items.title: Malfunction Reporting Patterns in Life-Supporting Versus Noninvasive Ventilators: A Stratified Text-Mining Analysis of the FDA Device MAUDE Database
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mechanical ventilators are essential life-support devices, yet evidence regarding device-related vulnerabilities remains limited compared with the extensive literature on human-factor-related adverse events. This study applied text-mining techniques to a large post-market surveillance database to examine ventilator malfunction reporting patterns and the effect of stratifying reports by device category. METHODS: Adverse event reports related to mechanical ventilators submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience database between January 2010 and December 2025 were stratified into life-supporting and noninvasive devices and analyzed using KH Coder. A random sample of the life-supporting reports was drawn for the primary analysis. Frequency analysis, co-occurrence network analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis, and correspondence analysis were performed. Device brand and year were used as external variables in the correspondence analysis. RESULTS: A total of 193,926 reports met the eligibility criteria, of which 177,641 were classified as malfunctions. The analyses were restricted to reports classified as malfunctions. Among life-supporting ventilators, the reported malfunctions spanned several broad themes, including power and battery failures, circuit-board and electronic faults, breathing-circuit and gas-delivery problems, and issues involving monitoring and control functions. Among noninvasive devices, reports were concentrated in terms associated with a single foam-related recall, as well as connector corrosion and patient-reported symptoms. Nearly 1 in 5 malfunction reports did not document a confirmed device failure during patient use. CONCLUSIONS: Text mining of ventilator-related adverse event reports revealed distinct reporting patterns across life-supporting and noninvasive devices. These findings are exploratory and do not establish the frequency or causes of device failure. Stratification of reports by device category helped prevent the reporting patterns of individual devices from being obscured by a single recall. This study demonstrates the potential value of combining post-market surveillance data with text-mining methods to support medical device safety surveillance.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence offers potential applications in wastewater monitoring, prediction, and operational decision support. However, selecting a model does not establish that factory managers and treatment operators can use it effectively. This conceptual article examines managerial readiness for artificial intelligence in Bangladesh's textile wastewater management. It brings together selected literature on organizational readiness, artificial intelligence capabilities, and wastewater applications, alongside Bangladesh-specific research and institutional reports. The article proposes six readiness domains: strategic commitment, managerial and operator knowledge, data stewardship, operational integration, investment and partnership capacity, and accountable decision making. It further distinguishes exploratory interest, supervised experimentation, routine decision support, and controlled operational integration as different adoption states. Four propositions explain how readiness may influence movement between these states and the translation of adoption into environmental performance. A proposed qualitative multiple-case design specifies evidence needed to examine these propositions, including decision histories, operational records, interviews across organizational levels, and observations of treatment routines. The framework is an analytical proposal rather than a validated measurement scale or report of completed fieldwork. Its contribution is to connect organizational preparation with the specific decisions, responsibilities, and verification practices required for textile wastewater management. Empirical research is needed to assess its relevance across factories with different resources and treatment arrangements.

items.title: Managing quality-oriented big data: a conceptual architecture for acquisition, fusion, and analytics in data-driven organizations
items.abstract: Data-driven organizations increasingly depend on large, heterogeneous, and fast-moving data to sustain the quality of their products, services, and processes. The transition toward data-driven organizational quality, often discussed under the label of Quality 4.0, has so far been examined mainly through a managerial lens. As a result, the data foundations of that transition remain fragmented and under-theorized. This Conceptual Analysis reframes quality-oriented big data as a first-class data management problem and proposes a layered conceptual architecture that organizes the lifecycle of such data across five interconnected layers: multi-source acquisition, integration and fusion, data quality assurance, analytics and knowledge extraction, and data governance and ethics. The central argument is that data quality operates as a central mediating construct linking big data capability to organizational quality outcomes: analytics improves organizational quality in large part to the extent that the underlying data are accurate, complete, consistent, timely, and well governed. Drawing on the data management, data quality, and machine learning systems literatures, the article specifies the constituent elements of each layer, the dependencies among them, and the failure modes that arise when the data foundation is neglected. Five propositions and a structured research agenda position the acquisition, fusion, quality assurance, and governance of quality-oriented big data as priorities for data mining and management research. The architecture offers a data-centric vocabulary for designing and evaluating the data infrastructures on which data-driven organizational quality ultimately depends.

items.title: Mapping knowledge management in Industry 4.0 era: a TCCM-guided bibliometric and thematic analysis
items.abstract: This study systematically maps and synthesizes the evolving literature on knowledge management (KM) in the context of Industry 4.0 (I4.0) by integrating bibliometric analysis with the Theory-Context-Characteristics-Method (TCCM) framework. Drawing on 93 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus (2018–2025), the study employs Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to analyze publication trends, intellectual structures, and thematic development, complemented by a structured TCCM-based synthesis. The findings reveal arapidly growing yet uneven field, dominated by perspectives on dynamic capabilities and absorptive capacity, with astrong concentration in manufacturing contexts and developed economies. Methodologically, the literature relies heavily on cross-sectional survey designs, while computational and longitudinal approaches remain limited. Thematic analysis identifies digital transformation, knowledge sharing, and organizational learning as core areas, whereas artificial intelligence, knowledge transfer, and governance remain underdeveloped. To address these gaps, the study proposes the Dynamic Knowledge Management Capability (DKMC) framework, conceptualizing KM as a technology-mediated capability shaped by human-AI interaction, real-time knowledge flows, and governance mechanisms. The study provides a transparent, theory-integrated synthesis and contributes to KM scholarship by incorporating AI-mediated knowledge processes and governance considerations, offering directions for future research and practice in digitally intensive environments.

items.title: Mapping the Research Landscape of Artificial Intelligence and Lifelong Learning: A Scientometric Analysis Using ScientoPy
items.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and lifelong learning has attracted growing educational, computational, and policy attention, yet its intellectual structure has not been mapped systematically. This study reports a scientometric analysis of the AI-lifelong learning literature indexed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection between 2014 and 2024. Records retrieved from both databases (N = 347) were merged and duplicated in ScientoPy, yielding 259 unique documents. Research momentum was quantified with three time-normalized indicators, average growth rate (AGR), average documents per year (ADY), and percentage of documents published in the last years (PDLY), across six analytical dimensions. Output grew from one document in 2014 to 116 in 2024; across the five principal document types (n = 220), 70.5% of records appeared in 2023-2024. Conference papers (41.3%) and journal articles (38.2%) predominated, with articles expanding fastest (AGR = 21.5; PDLY = 71.7%). Education & Educational Research recorded the highest normalized momentum among subject categories (AGR = 7.0; PDLY = 89.5%). Lifelong learning (n = 57) and artificial intelligence (n = 53) anchored the keyword field, while ChatGPT and Higher Education emerged entirely within the final two years. The United States led in volume (n = 57), whereas India (n = 29; PDLY = 89.7%) showed the strongest recent acceleration. Triangulating these indicators suggests, as an interpretive inference rather than a network-based measurement, that the corpus comprises three largely separate epistemic communities sharing a label but not a research program, framing an agenda for integrative, ethically grounded scholarship.

items.title: MAS-Bai: Linguistically Informed Adaptive Multi-Agent Translation for Bowen-Script Bai
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) remain unreliable for extremely low-resource languages whose writing systems conflict with high-resource pretraining priors. We study Bai-Chinese translation in the Bowen script, where Chinese characters are frequently borrowed phonetically rather than semantically, causing severe literal-translation hallucinations. We propose MAS-Bai, a linguistically informed adaptive multi-agent framework for Bowen-script Bai-Chinese translation. MAS-Bai routes each input through either a lightweight retrieval-translation path or a deeper philological path with etymological and syntactic agents, and uses cycle-consistency with a lightweight reverse translator as an inference-time reliability signal. We construct a 6,536-sentence Bai-Chinese corpus and evaluate on a 1,536-sentence test set. MAS-Bai achieves 16.23 BLEU and 62.15 COMET, improving over Standard RAG by 8.11 BLEU and 6.85 COMET. Forward LoRA, expert ablations and controlled routing experiments distinguish the roles of supervised adaptation, Bai-specific expertise and conditional routing. The largest gains occur on Bowen phonetic loans and divergent Bai word order, while human evaluation and reverse-verifier analyses support the automatic results.

items.title: Measuring Organizational Constructs in Large-Scale Text: An interpretive framework combining topic modeling and BERT
items.abstract: Measuring organizational constructs in large-scale unstructured text requires methods that preserve interpretive depth while enabling systematic, per-document classification. Structural Topic Modeling (STM) supports interpretive depth by surfacing patterns that inform construct operationalization, but its topic proportions are not designed as standalone per-document construct measures; transformer-based models such as BERT can scale measurement but require construct operationalization grounded in interpretive work. We address this challenge through a two-stage framework in which STM and BERT play structurally distinct roles. Coding schemes are developed through qualitative interpretation and STM analysis; BERT is then fine-tuned to apply these schemes across documents. We formalize two research approaches—construct-guided and pattern-discovery—that provide principled paths from different theoretical starting points toward a shared methodological endpoint: validated, auditable per-document construct measures. We illustrate the framework using more than 20,000 employee reviews. The framework supports iterative construct validation, using computational diagnostics to guide interpretive refinement and producing document-level measures suitable for theory-informed organizational analysis.

items.title: Mental Health, Fatigue and Training Needs Among Seafarers During the Red Sea Crisis
items.abstract: Global shipping carries over 80% of world trade, yet existing supply-chain-resilience theory models resilience at the level of the firm, node and network, without treating the workforce operating those nodes as a variable. This study addresses that gap using the 2023–2026 Red Sea/Houthi crisis as its empirical setting. A mixed-methods, pilot-scale design combined a 64-respondent self-report questionnaire of serving seafarers with thematic analysis of open-text responses. Seafarers exposed to Red Sea transits, Cape of Good Hope diversions, or a security incident rated STCW crisis-management training as significantly less adequate for conflict-area risk than unexposed seafarers, an effect that strengthened for incident-exposed respondents specifically. Open-text responses identified situational information and realistic scenario-based drills, rather than generic compliance training, as the specific gap, and a minority questioned seafarers' right to decline a high-risk voyage. These findings extend the conceptual framework linking geopolitical risk to operational resilience by distinguishing a training-competence pathway from a retention/psychological-contract pathway. The study contributes empirical evidence, gathered directly from an affected workforce, that the human factor is a measurable variable in geopolitical supply-chain-disruption theory, and derives practical and policy recommendations for STCW training content and seafarer consent protections.

items.title: Metabolically unhealthy normal weight in female domestic workers: unmasking hidden cardiometabolic risk beyond body mass index
items.abstract: Background: Metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUH-NW) describes individuals with a body mass index (BMI) within the normal range who nevertheless present cardiometabolic abnormalities. Evidence regarding this phenotype in specific female occupational populations remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of MUH-NW among female domestic workers and to characterize its associated anthropometric, clinical, biochemical, and lifestyle factors. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted using occupational health surveillance data from female domestic workers in Spain. The analysis included 3,344 women with a BMI of 18.5–24.9 kg/m². MUH-NW was defined as the presence of at least two of four abnormalities: elevated blood pressure (≥130/85 mmHg), fasting glucose ≥100 mg/dL, triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, and HDL-cholesterol Results: MUH-NW was identified in 352 women (10.5%; 95% CI, 9.5–11.6%), while 41.1% presented at least one metabolic abnormality. Low HDL-cholesterol (26.8%) and elevated blood pressure (18.2%) were the most frequent abnormalities. MUH-NW was associated with age (OR per year 1.13; 95% CI, 1.11–1.15), current smoking (OR 1.71; 95% CI, 1.31–2.22), and physical inactivity (OR 3.23; 95% CI, 2.21–4.71). Lack of Mediterranean diet adherence was not independently associated with MUH-NW after adjustment. Among anthropometric indices, BAI showed the strongest adjusted association (OR per SD 1.51; 95% CI, 1.32–1.73). However, individual anthropometric measures showed only modest discrimination. BAI had the highest AUC (0.680), but its performance was not significantly different from BMI (AUC 0.660; ΔAUC=0.021; DeLong p=0.164). Conclusions: Cardiometabolic abnormalities were present in a substantial proportion of normal-weight female domestic workers. MUH-NW was cross-sectionally associated with older age, current smoking, physical inactivity, and selected anthropometric measures. However, anthropometric indices alone showed limited ability to discriminate metabolic health status. These findings indicate that normal BMI does not necessarily coincide with a favorable cardiometabolic profile and support consideration of metabolic information alongside BMI when characterizing cardiometabolic health in normal-weight women. Given the cross-sectional design, the observed associations should not be interpreted as causal relationships.

items.title: MetaCurate: Evolving Curation Filters for High-Quality Agentic Coding Data
items.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning on agent trajectories is an effective way to improve coding agents, but selecting useful training examples requires more than identifying successful runs. A resolved patch may follow inefficient reasoning or unnecessary tool use, while a failed run may still contain useful intermediate steps. Training pipelines therefore rely on rules and qualitative assessments to filter trajectories, yet designing these filters typically requires substantial human expertise, and validating improvements through repeated training and evaluation is expensive. We introduce MetaCurate, a training-free framework that evolves executable trajectory curation filters using pairwise LLM judgments. Disagreements between the filter's rankings and the judge's preferences provide targeted feedback for jointly revising its rules, rubric, and aggregation policy. The resulting filter scores trajectories independently, so pairwise comparisons are required only during search. Starting from a blank filter, MetaCurate autonomously discovers a curation strategy that achieves competitive downstream performance without task-specific handwritten criteria. We validate downstream utility through controlled SFT experiments on our uncurated trajectory pool and the Nemotron v3 SWE dataset, with random selection and hand-authored filtering as baselines. In our experiments, MetaCurate achieves the highest mean SWE-Verified score among the compared methods, including hand-authored rule-based filtering and a training-loop baseline whose search costs 3.5x as much.

items.title: Mixed lignocellulosic biomass for continuous bioethanol production: logistics, process integration and biodesign
items.abstract: The increasing demand for renewable energy and the urgent need to mitigate climate change have driven global interest in bioethanol as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels. However, reliance on edible feedstocks such as corn, sugarcane or wheat has proven unsustainable due to food-fuel competition. In contrast, second-generation bioethanol production that utilizes lignocellulosic biomass primarily depends on a single biomass, limiting the continuous production because of seasonal variability and high production costs. Mixed lignocellulosic biomass (MLB) utilization has emerged as a promising strategy to address these challenges by integrating diverse agricultural residues, forestry waste, energy crops and industrial by-products within biorefineries. MLB provides supply stability, enhances enzymatic saccharification and minimizes inhibitor formation through synergistic buffering and compositional complementarity. This review comprehensively evaluates the significance of feedstock diversity, pretreatment strategies, enzymatic hydrolysis and fermentation approaches in MLB-based bioethanol production. It further examines process integration strategies, such as simultaneous saccharification and fermentation, consolidated bioprocessing and hybrid reactor systems for year-round operations. Techno-economic assessments demonstrate that MLB reduces the production costs, while life-cycle analyses confirm significant greenhouse gas mitigation potential. Despite these advantages, this study describes challenges in feedstock logistics, inhibitor management, strain robustness and process stability. Moreover, it outlines future directions that emphasize the roles of artificial intelligence and machine learning in feedstock blending, synthetic biology for robust microbial consortia and supportive policy frameworks to promote biomass aggregation. Overall, MLB represents a scalable and sustainable pathway for continuous second-generation bioethanol production, offering environmental, economic and technological advantages over single-feed approaches.

items.title: MLOps-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Production ML Engineering in Real Repositories
items.abstract: AI agents are increasingly expected to modify and maintain machine-learning systems in production, yet existing benchmarks primarily evaluate either competition-style ML experimentation or generic repository issue resolution. We introduce MLOps-Bench, a repository-grounded benchmark for production ML engineering. Unlike prior ML-agent benchmarks, MLOps-Bench evaluates executable lifecycle changes inside real ML repositories, spanning data pipelines, feature engineering, model training, model serving, monitoring, CI/CD and governance, and end-to-end integration. Each task is grounded in repository evidence and includes a natural-language requirement, oracle patch, plausible buggy baseline, fail-to-pass tests, pass-to-pass tests, and provenance metadata. The benchmark contains 212 validated tasks from 31 public ML repositories, with 636 fail-to-pass tests and 856 pass-to-pass tests. We evaluate six agents and find that the best system solves 31.2% of tasks while passing 68.7% of tests, showing that current agents often make partial progress but still fail production-relevant behavioral requirements. MLOps-Bench shifts agent evaluation beyond model building and issue fixing toward repository-native MLOps work where correctness depends on lifecycle reasoning, behavioral robustness, and preservation of existing system behavior.

items.title: MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning-to-Action Security of MLLM-Based Mobile Agents under Cross-Modal Consistency Injection
items.abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based mobile agents are rapidly evolving from conversational assistants into autonomous systems that perceive, reason over, and act on smartphone environments. This capability also exposes a new security risk: adversaries can embed malicious objectives in cross-application mobile content and steer agent behavior through indirect multimodal injection. Although prompt injection has been studied in desktop and web settings, its cross-modal properties in mobile ecosystems remain poorly understood, and existing security analyses are still limited. To close this gap, we introduce MobileInject, the first benchmark for evaluating mobile agents against multimodal injection attacks and reasoning-to-action security risks. MobileInject provides a high-fidelity interactive mobile evaluation framework covering 11 scenarios, 9 security-risk categories, and 108 executable risk instances. It further introduces Cross-Modal Consistency Injection to exploit corroboration across modalities, two enhanced attack methods, Multi-Role Collaborative Deception and Reasoning-Camouflage Injection, to intensify trust manipulation and reasoning hijacking, and a Reasoning Security Diagnosis Framework for fine-grained failure analysis. Systematic experiments show that mobile agents are broadly vulnerable to multimodal injection, and that many failures stem from reasoning hijacking at early stages. These findings establish MobileInject as a systematic cross-modal benchmark for studying and improving the security of mobile agents. Code release details are provided in the Appendix Open Science section.

items.title: Model Capacity Frontier: A Development Framework for LLM-Supported Social Simulation
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly incorporated into agent-based models (ABMs) on the premise that richer, context-sensitive human behavior can improve empirical fidelity. However, LLM-supported ABMs introduce an open-ended design space in which subtle modeling and configuration choices, such as prompt design and environment coupling, can substantially alter outcomes. Developing LLM-supported ABMs to simulate human collective behavior therefore requires navigating configuration sensitivity while identifying the limitations of the current model architecture. In this paper, we introduce the \textit{Model Capacity Frontier} (MCF), a framework that characterizes the empirical performance attainable by a specified architecture across its admissible configurations. In multi-objective settings, this capacity is represented by an estimated Pareto frontier obtained through systematic configuration exploration. We demonstrate MCF in crowd simulation of university commencement events with approximately 12,000 agents, using empirical movement data on temporal occupancy, spatial distribution, and flow direction. We first characterize the capacity of a conventional crowd model and then evaluate successive LLM-supported architectural extensions. In the process, MCF reveals which dimensions of attainable performance expand and which remain limited, providing empirical targets for refinement and re-evaluation. Initial LLM integration improves flow direction but degrades temporal occupancy and spatial distribution; subsequent architectural refinement of the LLM layer improves temporal occupancy and recovers spatial performance, while retaining much of the earlier gain in flow direction. Our case study shows how MCF guides the systematic architectural development of LLM-supported ABMs in configuration-sensitive, open-ended design spaces.

items.title: Model-Based Critical Pre-Crash Interaction Identification via Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.abstract: Historical pre-crash scenarios contain a sequence of vehicle-to-vehicle interactions, among which the critical pre-crash interaction is the one that most directly leads to the eventual collision. Identifying such critical interactions is important for uncovering potential safety risks in Autonomous Driving Systems (ADSs). However, this task remains challenging because the critical interaction is often embedded within numerous preceding interactions and needs to be distinguished by considering how the pre-crash scenario evolves over time. To address this challenge, we propose MICA, a model-based multi-agent approach for identifying critical pre-crash interactions from textual accident reports. Unlike existing LLM-based approaches that directly identify critical interactions from accident reports, MICA explicitly models the evolution of pre-crash interactions through multi-agent collaboration. Specialized LLM-based agents extract and validate relevant information to construct a Pre-crash Evolution Model, from which the critical interaction is identified by matching the modeled interactions to predefined pre-crash patterns. We evaluate MICA on 200 accident reports released by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV CA). The results demonstrate that MICA effectively identifies critical pre-crash interactions across different accident report data sources, scenario complexities, and underlying LLMs.

items.title: Monitor-Validity Failures: LLM Safety Evidence Paths at Evolving Framework Boundaries
items.abstract: Modern LLM applications rely on runtime monitors that inspect tool calls, traces, streams, detector outputs, and verifier inputs. This creates an interface-reliability problem: a framework path may remain operational while policy-relevant evidence never reaches its decision point. In one representative case, a regex detector returned a positive match, but the framework stranded the result before the block decision. This differs from jailbreaks and detector errors because the evidence is already recognized yet disconnected from enforcement. We study this repair-boundary signature with canary contracts: parent/fixed confirmation units that place a known payload only on the changed evidence surface and record monitor visibility together with the downstream decision for action-boundary cases. Applying the protocol to public framework repairs, we confirm 18 evidence-path failures across 11 LLM or agent safety project groups and four implementation ecosystems. Nine are established-boundary repairs, eight are new-surface policy-coverage gaps, and one is a boundary-only evidence case. Fourteen reach E1 enforcement boundaries: seven native action outcomes, six configured enforcement boundaries, and one synthetic-consumer consequence. The remaining cases affect verifier, safety-prompt, or observability channels. The cases form carrier, adapter, authority, and surface families and show how ordinary application behavior can remain intact while a safety-specific evidence path misses its decision. Exact revisions, deterministic outcomes, negative controls, and a frozen prospective audit document the confirmation rule. Monitor assumptions therefore need regression tests at the schemas, streams, tools, and adapters that frameworks evolve.

items.title: MTEdit: Packed Trajectories Beat Rollouts for Multi-Turn Image Editing
items.abstract: Multi-turn image editing aims to modify an image according to a sequence of instructions, making it better aligned with human-AI collaborative creation than single-turn editing. However, constructing high-quality multi-turn training data remains challenging, as conventional sequential rollout accumulates errors and introduces visual-quality drift across editing turns. To address this challenge, we introduce MTEdit, a multi-turn image editing dataset built through a pipeline centered on packed trajectory canvas (PTC) generation. By jointly generating multiple editing states within a unified visual context, this pipeline reduces visual-quality drift across turns. Covering both step-wise and context-aware editing scenarios, MTEdit comprises 500K multi-turn image editing trajectories, with up to 8 turns and an average of 5.38 turns per trajectory, making it one of the most extensive datasets for multi-turn image editing. We further introduce MTEdit-Bench, a benchmark designed to evaluate both scenarios by assessing models' ability to follow editing instructions, maintain content consistency, resist visual-quality drift, and effectively use historical context across turns. Using MTEdit, we fine-tune Qwen-Image-Edit-Causal to obtain Qwen-Image-MTEdit. On MTEdit-Bench, we evaluate a broad range of closed-source and open-source image editing models, including Qwen-Image-MTEdit. Experimental results show that Qwen-Image-MTEdit achieves the best performance among the evaluated open-source models, demonstrating the effectiveness of MTEdit in improving models' multi-turn image editing capabilities.

items.title: Multi-author style detection with stylistic embeddings
items.abstract: We investigate the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in multi-author style change detection. Using off-the-shelf LLMs or supervised fine-tuning solely within the target domain fails to yield effective features; for this reason, we propose cross-domain transfer learning with LLM-based embeddings fine-tuned for authorship verification. We fine-tune Mistral-7B embedding model and compare it with DeBERTa, used in the state-of-the-art (SOTA) systems in PAN-25 multi-author writing style analysis challenge. Results show that DeBERTa and Mistral excel in different user-generated text scenarios. We exploit this diversity by combining both embeddings, leading to more effective style change detection.

items.title: Multi-Criteria Decision-Making in Construction Management: A Bibliometric Analysis of the Integration of MCDM, BIM, and Artificial Intelligence (2015–2025)
items.abstract: The construction industry faces growing challenges that require better decision-making frameworks. Combining Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) with digital tools like Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a promising way forward. Yet their integration remains fragmented across research efforts, revealing a significant gap in theory and practice. As a result, their potential remains underutilized, limiting the development of flexible, data-driven decision-making tools for complex construction projects. This study conducts a systematic bibliometric analysis to map the development and structure of the MCDM-BIM-AI connection in construction management from 2015 to 2025. Using a PRISMA-compliant protocol, we analyzed 253 peer-reviewed articles from the Scopus database. Our approach combines performance analysis with science mapping through keyword co-occurrence networks and thematic evolution analysis across three time periods: 2015-2018, 2019-2021, 2022-2025, along with a country-level co-authorship network analysis. Our findings identify five main thematic clusters and show a significant increase in publications since 2019, mainly driven by the Asia-Pacific region. The analysis highlights a notable knowledge gap in the deep connection between BIM and AI within MCDM frameworks. The temporal mapping reveals three phases of evolution: pre-integration (2015-2018), Integration (2019-2021), and Innovation (2022-present), with AI and Machine Learning becoming key focus areas in the latest phase. The study suggests promising future directions for combining MCDM, BIM, and AI to promote more sustainable, data-driven, and resilient construction practices. It proposes a conceptual outline for the Intelligent Cognitive Decision Framework (ICDF), where BIM serves as a semantic data backbone, MCDM acts as the evaluation engine, and AI provides cognitive support for flexible, data-driven decision-making in construction 4.0 applications. This intellectual mapping offers researchers data-driven guidance for prioritizing impactful investigations, practitioners with technology investment plans that match research developments, and policymakers with informed priorities for research and development investment in underrepresented regions.

items.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
items.abstract: In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. An LLM judge can score the performance of the subagents, but these scores depend on the judge's own assessment of the quality of subagents' responses. We present MultiAgent-OPD, which combines on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning to jointly train a shared-parameter Leader-Searcher-Answerer team end to end. We first train a Teacher in a Searcher-Answerer workflow using answer correctness. During team training, the frozen Teacher scores student-generated search and summary tokens to provide local process supervision for the Searchers, while the Leader learns from team success and the Answerer from candidate correctness. Across seven datasets, the trained system reaches 38.68% macro avg@4, exceeding Prompted Critic by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL, the trained cascaded multiagent system, by 2.61 percentage points. The team also solves more questions within four attempts.

items.title: Multimodal Evidence-Based License Compliance Verification for KOGL Open Government Works on the Web
items.abstract: The reuse of open government works on the web has increased rapidly with the expansion of public data policies and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted content utilization. In Korea, Korea Open Government Licenses (KOGLs) permit the reuse of public works under conditions such as attribution, non-commercial use, and no-derivatives. However, these conditions are frequently violated or misunderstood in web pages, advertisements, social media posts, and reused digital content. Since compliance-related evidence is distributed across textual descriptions, captions, license metadata, embedded image text, visual changes, and page-level context, manual inspection, and single-modal analysis are not sufficient for scalable web-based compliance review. This paper proposes a multimodal evidence-based method for KOGL license compliance risk prediction in web environments. The proposed method combines textual context, KOGL metadata, optical character recognition (OCR) extracted image text, and visual features to classify four risk types: attribution risk, non-commercial use risk, no-derivatives risk, and false KOGL claim risk. A lightweight sequential context model captures the contextual flow of compliance-related cues, while the decision module produces both risk probabilities and evidence-based explanations. Experiments on a KOGL-oriented dataset show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy, macro-F1, and area under the curve (AUC) than text-only, image-only, and simple fusion baselines. The results demonstrate that multimodal web evidence improves compliance risk prediction and provides practical support for human review in public content management, open government data curation, and AI training data inspection.

items.title: Multiple Turns, Short Horizons: Measuring Effective-Horizon Compression in Jailbreaks
items.abstract: Multi-turn jailbreaks use feedback from a victim large language model to adapt their queries over several turns. However, once an effective trajectory has been found, it is unclear how much of the earlier query history is still needed. In this work, we study this by removing early attacker queries and running the remaining queries again in a new conversation while regenerating the victim's responses. We define the effective horizon as the shortest remaining query sequence that recovers the same attack progress. Empirically, we find that roughly half of the original query sequence is sufficient on average to recover the same attack progress. We call this phenomenon effective-horizon compression. We show that this shorter history can recover the best point reached during an unsuccessful attack and provide a better starting point for continuing the attack. It also helps identify which earlier queries should receive less learning signal during attacker training, and downweighting those queries improves performance. We further find that short reward-propagation windows preserve calibrated defense performance close to full-trajectory returns. These results show that multi-turn attacks can contain more queries than are needed to recover the progress reached later in the interaction.

items.title: Musculoskeletal disorders and ergonomic risk factors among petrochemical control room operators with health promotion and intervention strategies
items.abstract: This study aimed to assess musculoskeletal and ergonomic risk, identify demographic, occupational, lifestyle, and biomechanical characteristics associated with these outcomes, and develop and prioritize ergonomic intervention strategies for petrochemical control room operators. This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among 210 male control room operators from an Iranian petrochemical complex using census sampling. Data were collected using the Demographic/Occupational Questionnaire, Persian International Physical Activity Questionnaire (P-IPAQ), Persian Örebro Musculoskeletal Pain Screening Questionnaire (P-ÖMSQ), and Persian Ergonomic Screening and Priority Tool (P-ESPT), complemented by objective postural and plantar pressure assessments. The P-ÖMSQ was used to classify participants according to P-ÖMSQ risk categories, with scores ≥ 90 categorized as moderate-to-high risk. Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software, version 20.0, with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression. A P-ÖMSQ score within the moderate-to-high risk categories (≥ 90) was observed in 27% of participants, while 78% were classified as having moderate-to-high ergonomic risk. Multivariable logistic regression showed that older age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.02–1.17, p = 0.014), higher body mass index (BMI) (aOR = 1.15, 95% CI = 1.04–1.27, p = 0.006), and longer job tenure (aOR = 1.98, 95% CI = 1.01–3.89, p = 0.047) were independently associated with higher odds of being classified in the moderate-to-high-risk P-ÖMSQ category. Lower physical activity was significantly associated with a higher prevalence of forward head posture, thoracic hyperkyphosis, lateral pelvic tilt, and pes planus ( p < 0.05). Objective biomechanical abnormalities were also significantly associated with higher P-ÖMSQ-based and P-ESPT-based risk categories ( p < 0.05). Based on the study findings, 20 ergonomic intervention strategies were proposed and prioritized through a stakeholder-informed participatory process. Older age, higher body mass index, and longer job tenure were associated with higher odds of being classified in the moderate-to-high-risk P-ÖMSQ category, while lower physical activity was associated with selected postural abnormalities among petrochemical control room operators. Several objective biomechanical abnormalities were also associated with P-ÖMSQ-based and P-ESPT-based risk categories. These findings may inform the prioritization of workplace ergonomic interventions; however, the proposed interventions were not evaluated in the present study, and their effectiveness should be assessed in future longitudinal and interventional studies.

items.title: NATURAL LANGUAGE DATABASE QUERY AND ANALYTICS AGENT
items.abstract: Colleges record semester results in spreadsheets, and answering even a simple question about them, such as how one section performed compared with another, usually means filtering and calculating by hand or writing SQL. This paper presents the Natural Language Database Query and Analytics Agent, a system that lets non-technical users ask such questions in plain English. The agent supplies the schema of a relational database to a large language model, which writes a SQL query. The query is checked, executed in read-only mode, corrected using the database error message if it fails, and the result is returned as text, a table or a chart. The design is applied to the Information Science and Engineering result sheets of 206 students over three semesters (IV, V and VI). Example questions are run against the prepared database, and their answers are reported as ground truth for future testing, along with data-quality problems found in the source sheets. The measured accuracy of the model-generated queries is left for future work.

items.title: Navigating GenAI in the workplace: skills transformation & tension
items.abstract: By automating the content creation process, Generative AI is reshaping creative work, but its impact on knowledge workers remains underexplored, which this study seeks to examine. Drawing on in-depth interviews with 20 knowledge workers, this study examines what is being transformed in the workplace and how these shifts are being perceived by the knowledge workers who use GenAI. Using Social Shaping of Technology (SST) as a conceptual lens to understand the interaction between technology and knowledge workers, the study finds that participants perceived GenAI as an efficient tool that provides cognitive relief and enhances productivity during times of resource constraint. Tensions also arose around authenticity, creativity, a sense of fulfillment, and the perception of effort. The adoption of GenAI has created downstream labor and demand for new skills as it shifts knowledge workers’ roles away from creator to editor/fact-checker while creating tension as participants balance their desire for efficiency with fears of diminished creativity and domain knowledge, skills atrophy, and threats to content ownership.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Network Flow-Based IoT Botnet Behavior Detection and Explanation Using Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: IoT botnets generate diverse network behaviors, including scanning, command-and-control communication, and distributed denial-of-service activity. Traditional machine learn-ing models can achieve high detection accuracy using engineered network-flow features, but they often provide limited behav-ioral explanation. This work presents a network flow-window framework for IoT botnet behavior detection and explanation using both conventional machine learning baselines and a multi-agent large language model (LLM) reasoning pipeline. The proposed approach aggregates Zeek network flows into fixed-size behavioral windows and uses two IoT-23 scenarios: a scanning-dominated scenario for behavior-window construction and a main three-class scenario containing benign, C&C, and DDoS behavior. For the second scenario, non-leakage machine learning baselines achieved strong performance, with XGBoost and Random Forest reaching 99.42% accuracy using only network-derived window features. The multi-agent LLM pipeline, consisting of a behavior analyst, threat classifier, and judge agent, achieved 98.24% classifier accuracy and 97.65% judge accuracy over valid parsed outputs on a balanced 342-window evaluation set. When one invalid JSON response is counted as an automated failure, the end-to-end judge accuracy is 97.37%. Error analysis showed that most remaining errors occurred in behaviorally ambiguous cases, particularly benign windows with high-volume one-way DNS-like traffic and low-volume C&C windows mixed with benign-looking NTP traffic. The results suggest that conventional ML remains highly effective for structured classification, while multi-agent LLM reasoning adds interpretable evidence-based analysis and supports more transparent investigation of IoT botnet behavior.

items.title: New requirements for medical device safety monitoring: key challenges for healthcare organizations.
items.abstract: Relevance. Medical device safety monitoring is one of the consistently and strictly controlled mandatory requirements imposed on healthcare organizations. Objective: to analyze the new Procedure for the implementation of medical device safety monitoring and the new Procedure for reporting adverse events in the field of medical device circulation with a view to identifying the new tasks now facing healthcare organizations. Results. It is noted that the new orders of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation have significantly clarified and detailed the requirements for information, the collection, processing, and recording of which are carried out during medical device safety monitoring. This includes, inter alia, data transmitted by software employing artificial intelligence technologies that constitutes a medical device; information on adverse events in the field of medical device circulation in other states; and information contained in an adverse event report. Attention is drawn to the increased significance of the Classification of adverse events related to the circulation of medical devices. Conclusion. Healthcare organizations should pay special attention to the fact that the identification of adverse events in the field of medical device circulation must now be carried out in strict accordance with the Classification of adverse events approved by Order No. 4513 of the Federal Service for Surveillance in Healthcare (Roszdravnadzor) dated May 20, 2021. In accordance with the new Procedure for the implementation of medical device safety monitoring, each healthcare organization is required to appoint an official responsible for organizing the work of collecting information in order to ensure the safe use of medical devices and to establish the procedure for this work.

items.title: NL2SQL with Iterative Self-Refinement
items.abstract: Bridging the gap between human intent and machine logic remains a critical challenge in data access for non-technical users, yet Large Language Models (LLMs) remain unreliable: they hallucinate schema elements, generate syntactically invalid queries, or fail to capture user intent. These limitations are especially critical in domains such as insurance, where KPIs, regulatory constraints, and legacy relational systems demand high precision. We introduce a multi-agent, persona-driven NL2SQL framework that combines (1) domain relevance detection, (2) schema-grounded knowledge construction, (3) KPI-aware SQL synthesis, (4) syntax-level self-repair using sqlite execution feedback, and (5) semantic consistency checking via SQL-to-NL reverse engineering. Our system significantly reduces query hallucination and improves semantic fidelity compared to direct LLM prompting. Evaluated on 60 queries (50 from a HuggingFace text-to-SQL dataset and 10 custom domain queries), the system achieves 90% correctness using Mistral across seven coordinated LLM calls showing that this approach can substantially increase the reliability of NL2SQL pipelines in high-stakes environments.

items.title: Not so Tense, but Becoming Boring! A Study on Human-Machine Interaction and Metro Drivers’ Safety Performance
items.abstract: As automation reshapes work, employees increasingly interact with intelligent systems rather than perform core tasks directly. Drawing on Campion’s job design perspective and Affective Events Theory, this study examines the double-edged effects of human-machine interaction (HMI) on metro drivers’ safety performance. We propose that HMI enhances safety compliance and safety participation by reducing job tension. However, HMI may also undermine these safety outcomes by increasing work-related boredom. We further identify organizational readiness for change as a key boundary condition. Using three-wave, multi-source data from 454 metro drivers and 69 supervisors in China, we find that HMI improves safety performance through reduced job tension but undermines it through increased work-related boredom. In addition, organizational readiness for change strengthens the former pathway while weakening the latter. These findings extend HMI research by highlighting affective mechanisms, advance a job design perspective on automation-enabled work, and underscore the importance of organizational context.

items.title: Nursing leadership and performance metrics in artificial intelligence integrated gastrointestinal surgical care: A narrative review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being integrated into gastrointestinal and complex surgical care, yet its practical impact on nursing work remains insufficiently defined.This narrative review examines how nursing leadership can support the safe use of AI across perioperative pathways and how its effects can be evaluated through measurable nursing-sensitive outcomes.Literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, with emphasis on peer-reviewed studies, systematic reviews, guidelines, consensus statements, and implementation frameworks relevant to gastrointestinal surgery, perioperative nursing, clinical decision support, and AI.The review focuses on preoperative assessment, intraoperative coordination, postoperative surveillance, and discharge planning in high-acuity surgical settings.Particular attention is given to workflow efficiency, response times, early recognition of complications, risk-stratified care, documentation quality, interdisciplinary communication, cognitive workload, and patient safety.The proposed framework is intended as a practical, non-validated structure for future evaluation rather than as an established measurement instrument.Its use will require prospective validation and adaptation to local staffing, digital infrastructure, resources, and clinical workflows.AI should therefore be judged not only by predictive performance, but by whether it helps nurses recognize risk earlier, communicate concerns clearly, and deliver safer perioperative care.

items.title: Occupational determinants of burnout among Chinese anesthesiologists: a multicenter cross-sectional study based on the Job Demands–Resources model
items.abstract: Burnout among healthcare professionals is an important occupational health concern that may negatively affect individual well-being, healthcare workforce sustainability, and quality of care. Anesthesiologists are particularly vulnerable to burnout due to high workload, clinical responsibility, time pressure, and irregular working schedules. However, the occupational mechanisms underlying burnout among anesthesiologists remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the associations of job demands and job resources with burnout among Chinese anesthesiologists based on the Job Demands–Resources (JD–R) model. A multicenter cross-sectional survey was conducted among anesthesiologists from 72 hospitals across 22 provinces in China from June 16 to June 30, 2026. The ethics exemption was approved on June 11, 2026. Participants were recruited using a multicenter purposive sampling method and completed a general information questionnaire, a JD–R model-based questionnaire, and the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS). Burnout status was assessed according to established criteria. Differences in demographic and occupational characteristics between burnout and non-burnout groups were examined using chi-square tests. Spearman correlation analyses were performed to evaluate associations between job demands, job resources, and burnout dimensions. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to identify factors independently associated with burnout. All statistical analyses were performed using R software and RStudio (version 2026.01.2 + 418). Among the 698 anesthesiologists included in the analysis, 324 (46.4%) met the criteria for burnout. Significant differences between burnout and non-burnout groups were observed in sex, age, educational level, marital status, professional title, work experience, weekly working hours, and number of night shifts. Higher job demands were positively correlated with emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment, whereas greater job resources showed negative correlations with all three burnout dimensions. In the fully adjusted model (Model 4), participants aged 31–40 years (vs. ≤ 30 years: OR = 9.677, 95% CI 2.287–40.940) and 41–50 years (OR = 8.305, 95% CI 1.705–40.463) had higher odds of burnout, whereas married participants (vs. unmarried: OR = 0.221, 95% CI 0.096–0.508) and those with more than 10 years of work experience (vs. < 5 years: OR = 0.178, 95% CI 0.050–0.638) had lower odds. At the sample mean of job resources, higher job demands were associated with higher odds of burnout (OR = 1.287, 95% CI 1.228–1.350); at the sample mean of job demands, higher job resources were associated with lower odds (OR = 0.850, 95% CI 0.808–0.893). Their interaction was statistically significant (OR = 1.009, 95% CI 1.003–1.016, P = 0.006). Burnout is relatively common among Chinese anesthesiologists and represents an important occupational health challenge. Consistent with the JD–R model, higher job demands were associated with increased likelihood of burnout, whereas greater job resources were associated with reduced likelihood after adjustment for demographic and occupational factors. These findings may inform future evaluations of organizational strategies that optimize workload and strengthen workplace resources.

items.abstract: Background: Traffic police personnel perform physically demanding duties involving prolonged standing, intermittent walking, repetitive weight-bearing, and exposure to variable road surfaces. These occupational conditions may contribute to foot discomfort, lower-limb fatigue, and musculoskeletal symptoms. Foot posture, anthropometric characteristics, standing duration, and occupational footwear are important factors to consider when evaluating foot health. Objective: This review examines the existing literature on occupational foot health, with particular emphasis on foot posture, prolonged standing, footwear comfort, body mass index (BMI), foot pain, and functional disability among traffic police personnel and other occupational groups with similar work demands. Review approach: A narrative review approach was used to organize relevant literature on foot posture assessment, occupational standing, footwear characteristics, and musculoskeletal health. Published clinical assessment studies and occupational health reviews were considered. The review emphasizes the relevance of these findings to traffic police personnel in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, India. Review findings: The literature indicates that prolonged standing is associated with several adverse health outcomes, including lower-limb discomfort and fatigue. Footwear characteristics, such as cushioning, sole hardness, fit, and insole design, may influence foot comfort and mechanical loading. Standardized tools, including the Foot Posture Index-6 (FPI-6), can support quantitative assessment of standing foot posture. However, static foot posture, pain intensity, and functional disability represent different outcomes and should be assessed separately. The available evidence does not establish that age, BMI, or standing duration necessarily causes a particular foot posture in traffic police personnel. Conclusion: Occupational foot health should be considered an important component of preventive health assessment among traffic police personnel. Future research in Bareilly should investigate foot posture, footwear comfort, standing duration, BMI, pain, and functional limitations using standardized assessment methods. Evidence from appropriately designed studies may inform occupational health screening and further evaluation of preventive strategies.

items.title: OfficeTown: Generative Organizations for Evolving Agent Intelligence
items.abstract: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. From a natural-language description of an organization's purpose and activities, OfficeTown initializes an organization whose members coordinate work, delegate bounded assignments to assistant agents, and review their deliverables. Artifacts, decisions, and unresolved matters persist and shape subsequent work, while responsibilities and permissions determine what each member can see and do. We curate work requests, their context, and review feedback into executable resources for evaluation and learning. We construct OfficeTown Bench with 406 tasks and 4,836 evaluation criteria from 23 simulated organizations across eight professional domains, incorporating domain-expert feedback. Frontier-model evaluations reveal substantial remaining headroom. Supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation on OfficeTown data substantially improve Qwen3.5-9B on external professional-work benchmarks, including GDPval. Supplementary evaluations show that the principal--assistant harness achieves higher scores than the single- and multi-agent baselines tested. These results highlight the value of organizational simulation in generating work-grounded data and environments for the continued development of generalist agents.

items.title: Oh doughnuts, it's the variance! A visual metaphor for the variance, standard deviation, and related quantities
items.abstract: Despite the rise of artificial intelligence, human intuition endures as both a foundation for education and also (for now) a primarily human experience. We re-examine a formula for the sum of squares that is sometimes set aside because of possible numerical issues. The formula can be used to create square doughnuts, a delicious regional favorite. The variance becomes the dough, and we can examine the variance by either comparing doughnuts or by making different sizes of doughnuts with the same amount of dough. In doing so, we provide a new visualization of a cornerstone formula, understandable by students at almost any level. We further provide insight into related topics such as the coefficient of variation as well as a visualization of when numerical issues are likely to be problematic. We also provide a new vocabulary for understanding the variance formula, with `dough' and `hole' taking the place of less edible concepts from the typical recipe.

items.title: One Provider, Several Plans: The Ground Handling Provider in Nested Aviation Emergency Response Arrangements
items.abstract: When an aircraft accident or another serious emergency occurs at an airport, an independent ground handling provider may work under several emergency arrangements at once: the aerodrome emergency plan, the emergency response plans of the airlines it serves, its own plan and the emergency provisions of occupational health and safety law. This paper examines how public regulatory and guidance documents position the provider within these nested arrangements. A document analysis of 21 international, European, national and industry sources, recorded with their legal status and access level, was combined with research on interorganisational coordination in emergencies. Each document was coded for nine emergency functions, distinguishing explicit, implicit, not stated and not assessable provisions; only the third category was treated as evidence of absence. The European acceptable means of compliance and guidance material for ground handling organisations, issued in 2025, now address the provider directly: they require corporate and station level emergency response plans, coordination with aerodrome and aircraft operators, support for or substitution of the aircraft operator's plan, contact arrangements, training and testing. Precedence of aerodrome procedures is stated for listed operational aspects. In the documents reviewed in full, no provision was found on how a provider that serves several airlines should allocate staff and equipment committed to more than one plan, and functions such as passenger information, family assistance and dangerous goods information remain assigned to the airline without provisions on their performance through an agent. The paper argues that the main unresolved problem is the multiple commitment of the same resources, and that questions of authority must be separated into procedure, command, employer duty, delegated tasks and resource allocation. Implications for handling agreements, aerodrome plans and multiairline exercises are discussed

items.title: Optimization of Renewable Energy Systems Using Artificial Intelligence in Nigeria: A Focus on Generation and Distribution
items.abstract: Nigeria’ s energy sector is marred by structural inefficiencies, unreliable grid infrastructure, and an overdependence on fossil fuels, resulting in inadequate electricity access and persistent blackouts. Despite possessing vast renewable energy resources—particularly solar and wind—the country continues to underutilize them due to technical, financial, and regulatory barriers. This study examines the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing these challenges and optimizing renewable energy generation, distribution, and management. Employing a qualitative secondary research methodology, the study analyzes peerreviewed literature, national policy documents, and global case studies to evaluate the applicability of AI technologies such as machine learning, neural networks, and predictive analytics within the Nigerian context. Case studies of solar farms, wind energy forecasting, smart grid operations, and urban load management illustrate how AI can enhance forecasting accuracy, improve grid reliability, reduce operational costs, and support decentralized energy access in rural areas. However, the adoption of AI faces significant hurdles, including high implementation costs, limited technical expertise, and a lack of robust data infrastructure. To overcome these barriers, the study recommends strategic public-private partnerships, targeted capacity-building programs, supportive data policy frameworks, and pilot initiatives to demonstrate feasibility. The integration of AI into Nigeria’ s renewable energy systems offers a promising pathway toward achieving national energy security, sustainability, and socioeconomic development.

items.title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
items.abstract: Can large language model (LLM) agents deliver expert-level operations research (OR) solutions directly from original client materials, without prior expert reformulation? Existing OR benchmarks typically begin with self-contained descriptions or predefined optimization tasks, underrepresenting the translation of original business materials into professionally validated solutions. We introduce OR-License, an end-to-end benchmark of 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios from paid OR engagements totaling USD 3.68 million. It preserves original requirements, input data, deliverable formats, and information boundaries after de-identification. To study information acquisition, we introduce ORSim, a controlled client simulator that discloses business facts without supplying OR expertise. Hidden evaluation checks feasibility and compares objective quality against original expert solutions accepted by clients before benchmark construction. Deployment-Adjusted Quality (DAQ) averages expert-relative quality across instances, assigning zero to infeasible deliveries. Across 11 frontier LLMs using coding-agent harnesses, several exceed the expert reference in conditional objective quality, but none matches its DAQ; the strongest primary Claude Code configuration achieves 88.39% strict feasibility and a DAQ of 0.87 against the expert reference of 1. Client information acquisition extends beyond clarification into solution development and validation, with some later stages showing higher confirmed issue-resolution proportions. Trajectory analysis identifies formulation and implementation failures, while task-equalized research-chain completion rates range from 24% to 45% across models on evaluable tasks. These findings motivate sustained information-gap resolution, faithful problem formulation, and evidence-linked self-improvement for reliable long-horizon agents.

items.title: Out of Support, Not Out of Reach: In-Context Learning with Unsupported Instructions and Composed Tasks
items.abstract: In-Context Learning (ICL) enables pretrained LLMs to adapt to downstream tasks from a small set of input-output demonstrations, without parameter updates. Yet existing theory primarily explains ICL as identifying a latent task already represented in pretraining, leaving unclear whether ICL can succeed when either the instruction or the target task falls outside the pretraining support. We develop a theoretical framework under mild assumptions that separates these two forms of distribution shift. For target tasks represented in pretraining, we show that demonstrations can identify the task and reduce sensitivity to pretrain-supported prompt templates as their number increases. For an unsupported instruction, we show that under a fixed model-induced reference extension, demonstration evidence can dominate an $N$-independent instruction shift while preserving the exponential identification rate. We then use the same ICL framework as an interpretive lens for long-horizon target tasks that are not represented in pretraining but admit a plan that decomposes them into pretraining-supported subtasks. Applying the supported-task analysis step by step yields a standard accumulated-error bound and clarifies how invoking familiar subtasks along an intermediate-state trajectory can avoid directly selecting the unsupported complete task. Together, our results characterize when demonstrations, instructions, and task decomposition can support ICL beyond the corresponding pretraining supports.

items.title: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
items.abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring offers actionable evidence for oversight AI systems, with the potential to enable early detection and intervention. However, existing approaches are focused on specific tasks, whereas the regulation of AI, particularly reasoning models, requires monitoring a broader range of tasks. We introduce Factor for CoT monitoring, a strategy that supports customizing monitoring requirements in the prompt, which enables a single monitor to cover different tasks by relying on different factors. Furthermore, we introduce two types of factors, fine-grained and coarse-grained (e.g., monitoring whether a specific email address has been leaked versus monitoring privacy leakage), to accommodate diverse user monitoring needs. Based on this, we develop a CoT monitor named OwlSight that relies solely on factor to monitor behaviors related to multiple dimensions, including capability, safety, and trustworthiness. Experiments across 15,971 reasoning trajectories show that OwlSight surpasses general-purpose LLMs by 1.32-30.57 and 11.71-27.81 points at fine and coarse granularity, respectively, and achieves state-of-the-art results on OpenAI's CoT monitorability benchmark. It also generalizes to unseen models' CoTs and remains robust to Factor rephrasings, CoT compression, and obfuscation, offering a promising paradigm for CoT monitoring that can contribute to the oversight of frontier AI.

items.title: PairSight: Characterizing and Predicting Operator-Level Interference in GPU Sharing for DNN Inference
items.abstract: Serving DNN inference is costly, yet a single task seldom saturates both the compute units and the memory bandwidth of a GPU. GPU sharing raises utilization by co-locating several tasks on one GPU, at the cost of interference among them. Existing systems estimate this interference with binary compute-memory rules, standalone scaling curves, or model-level predictors. However, these estimates rest on a limited understanding of interference. They leave the software and hardware properties of co-located operators largely unexplored and give no slowdown prediction that is both interpretable and accurate. We conduct an operator-level study of interference under SM partitioning and use hardware counters to trace it to contention on the shared memory path, where the slowdown depends jointly on both co-located operators. Based on these findings, we propose PairSight, a hardware-aware interference predictor that learns how the hardware behaviors of co-located tasks interact and predicts the latency of each task before co-location. On six DNN models including LLMs, PairSight predicts latency under sharing with 4.3% mean error, against 19.0% for a compute-memory intensity rule, and adapts to unseen models and inputs with a few samples.

items.title: ParetoChat: An LLM-Based Interface for Interactive Multi-Objective Optimization
items.abstract: Multi-objective optimization models are often deployed in settings where decision makers (DMs) must balance some conflicting criteria. In practice, however, stakeholders must translate their qualitative preferences between different criteria into numerical weights, priorities, or reference points required by optimization methods, which can be difficult to specify and interpret. This paper proposes \emph{ParetoChat}, an LLM (large language model)-based expert-agent interface for interactive multi-objective optimization. The agent translates natural-language user input into structured scalarization parameters, invokes an optimization system, presents candidate solutions, and iteratively elicits feedback. We describe a multi-agent architecture that separates input processing, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) expertise, solution presentation, and feedback processing. We then present a simulation study using an LLM-based DM agent and benchmark ParetoChat against interactive methods implemented in DESDEO, including reference-point and NIMBUS methods. The computational experiments on multi-objective binary knapsack and set-partitioning instances show that ParetoChat can guide the search efficiently toward solutions that match the DM's preferences. An application to historical courier-order assignment instances illustrates how users can explore objective extremes and intermediate trade-offs through natural-language requests. The results indicate that LLM agents may provide a practical interaction layer between business stakeholders and optimization tools.
